topic: a robot who wanted a friend
text:
Eli was a robot. Eli wanted a friend. He sat on a bench and watched the kids play. He waved. The kids ran away. Eli felt sad.

That night, Eli saw a small green light. It was far away, across the water. It blinked once. Then again. Eli looked at it for a long time.

The next day, a girl sat by Eli. Her name was May. She said, "Hello, robot." Eli said, "Hello." They played with a ball. May laughed. Eli felt happy.

But at night, Eli saw the green light again. It was little and far. It blinked and blinked. Eli reached his hand out. He could not touch it. It was too far away.

Eli looked at May's window. Her room was dark. Then he looked back at the green light. He did not know why he wanted it. He just did.

May came back the next day. They played again. Eli had a friend now. But still, at night, he watched the green light across the water. It blinked, and he wanted.

topic: a clock on the kitchen wall
text:
Mira had a clock on the kitchen wall. It was round and white. It went tick, tick, tick. Mira liked the clock. It told her when to eat. It told her when to sleep.

One day Mira sat at the table. She ate her bread. She looked at the clock. The clock said it was late. But out the window, Mira saw a small green light. It was far away, across the street. It was very small and very green.

Mira looked at the clock again. Tick, tick. Then she looked back at the light. It did not move. It just stayed there, green and far.

Mira wanted to touch it. But it was too far. She could not go now. Her mom said, "Eat your bread, Mira."

Mira ate her bread. She looked at the clock. Tick, tick. She looked at the green light one more time. It was still there. Then Mira went to bed. The clock said good night, tick, tick.

topic: a boy building a rain catcher
text:
Tom wanted to catch the rain. He put a big pot on the grass. He put a little cup next to it. He made a paper funnel and taped it on top.

"Rain will come," said Tom. "Then we have water."

He sat on the step and waited. The sky was gray and soft. No rain yet.

Far away, across the field, Tom saw a small green light. It was at the end of the old dock. It blinked slow, like a tiny eye. Tom looked at it for a while. Then he looked back at his pot.

"Rain first," he said.

He checked the funnel. He checked the cup. He pulled a leaf out of the pot.

The green light stayed on. It was far, but Tom could see it. He did not go to it. He had work to do.

Then a drop hit the pot. Then more. Tap, tap, tap. Tom smiled.

"I caught it," he said.

The green light blinked once more across the water. Tom waved at it, just a little, and went inside.
